summary:
Lunar Planner is a web app that helps mission planners, educators and the public decide where and when to land at the Moon's south pole. There, the Sun skims the horizon, crater rims cast shadows for days, and Earth often disappears behind the terrain. Existing tools give Sun and Earth positions but are hard to use.

Users pick one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions, a south-pole site, or draw their own area. They set a search period, a mission length, and simple or advanced needs for power, heat and Earth contact. Lunar Planner scores every possible mission window, says plainly whether each window meets every need and why not, and maps the best spots for the base, solar panels and antenna on a 3D Moon. A horizon chart shows the Sun and Earth against the real terrain skyline, and a street-level view lets anyone stand on a crater rim and play the sky forward.

It is built on NASA's 5 m LOLA terrain and Artemis III regions, plus JPL's SPICE ephemeris and Horizons.
details:
Lunar Planner is a web app for choosing where and when to land at the Moon's south pole. A user picks one of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions, a south-pole site, or draws an area; sets a search period, a mission length, and simple needs for power, heat and Earth contact. For every spot it computes Sun and Earth positions (NASA JPL SPICE), checks them against the real terrain horizon (NASA LOLA 5 m data) and models surface temperature (Hayne et al. 2017). It ranks every mission window, says plainly whether each meets every need and why not, and maps the best spots for the base, solar panels and antenna on a 3D Moon. A horizon chart shows the Sun and Earth against the terrain skyline; users can compare all nine Artemis III regions and stand on a crater rim to play the sky forward.

Impact: planners can shortlist sites and dates in seconds instead of days, and students can see why polar landings are hard.

Tools: Python (FastAPI, NumPy, SpiceyPy, Shapely, rasterio), TypeScript, React, CesiumJS, PostgreSQL, Docker. Code, documentation and presentation were developed with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude Code by Anthropic).

Creativity: it searches time and place together and places each piece of equipment where it works best. We considered scientific honesty (stated limits, checked against JPL Horizons), realistic equipment height, speed and plain language.
